Dan Bradbury, an assistant professor of marketing, is conducting the research as artificial intelligence increasingly shifts from systems that answer individual prompts to autonomous agents capable of carrying out longer, multistep processes. [...] For a single task, those costs may be manageable. But Bradbury said the economics can change when AI is used repeatedly for research, data analysis or other organizational workflows.

The issue is not simply whether local AI is cheaper, however, Bradbury said. [...] A local artificial intelligence workflow can reduce or eliminate the need to transmit those materials to an external model provider because the model and associated files can remain on hardware controlled directly by the researcher, he said.

Local AI also changes the economics of intensive AI use.
